newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo share rises 3.5 SKR on Q1 report.
newsitem.headline: Volvo share rises 3.5 SKR on Q1 report.

text.p: Shares in Swedish automotive group AB Volvo rose at the Stockholm Stock Exchange open on Wednesday after the company posted a 60 percent rise in first quarter operating profit to 1.89 billion crowns.
At 0725 GMT, the share was up 3.5 crowns at 197, while the bourse's general index rose 0.64 percent to 2,635.63.
"Volvo's earnings were decent and the share is probably rising in a recovery after being depressed by an article in the Gothenburg Post recently," a trader said.

The newspaper reported that internal company documents showed Volvo expected to post an operating profit of six billion crowns this year, while aiming for an operating profit of 10 billion crowns in the longer term.
The group said positive development continued.
"Volvo Cars is in a period of fast product renewal," said Volvo's chief executive Soren Gyll in the first quarter report.
Volvo Cars sales rose 18 percent in the first three months ending March 31 to 23.07 billion crowns with operating profit of 1.07 billion crowns against a loss of 191 million crowns a year earlier.
